A time-based debouncer has a 30 ms interval (a change is accepted when the raw level has been steady for more than 30 ms). The raw input last changes at t = 40 ms and is sampled every 1 ms. At which t does the stable level change?
questions.explanation: The first sample with t - 40 > 30 is t = 71.

questions.prompt: Why must a variable shared between an ISR and loop() be declared volatile?
options: It makes multi-byte reads atomic.
It moves the variable to flash to save RAM.
Stops the compiler caching it in a register.
It lets the ISR call delay() safely.
questions.explanation: Without volatile the compiler may keep the value in a register and loop() never sees the ISR update. It does not make multi-byte reads atomic.

questions.prompt: A decoder sees the transition 11 to 00. What does it mean and what should the decoder do?
options: A missed edge: log an error, do not guess.
A forward double step, so add +2 to the count.
A reverse double step, so add -2 to the count.
A normal forward step, so add +1 to the count.
questions.explanation: Two bits changed at once, so an edge was missed and the direction cannot be known. Count an error and add nothing.

questions.prompt: A Timer1 ISR toggles pin 8 once per interrupt and the interrupt rate is 2 kHz. What does a logic analyzer show on pin 8?
options: 4 kHz
2 kHz
500 Hz
1 kHz
questions.explanation: One toggle per interrupt means one full period (high and low) per two interrupts: 1 kHz.

questions.prompt: An ESP32 must count 80 000 encoder edges per second on each of two encoders. Which structure is best?
options: A pin-change ISR on every pin with Serial debugging.
Hardware pulse counter (PCNT), quadrature mode.
Polling in loop() with delay(1).
A 50 ms debounce on both channels.
questions.explanation: The interrupt load would exceed 100 %. Hardware pulse counters count edges with no CPU time.

questions.prompt: Which situation most clearly favours FreeRTOS tasks over a super-loop with a timer tick?
options: One LED blinking at 1 Hz with nothing else running.
Reading one potentiometer once every second.
1 kHz control, 50 Hz IMU, blocking Wi-Fi upload.
A button that toggles a relay when pressed.
questions.explanation: Activities with different rates and priorities, some waiting on slow I/O, benefit from tasks and queues; a single tick is enough for a few simple jobs.

questions.prompt: Which debouncing approach needs no CPU time and works with any firmware?
options: An RC filter feeding a Schmitt input.
A 50 ms delay() after each detected press.
Reading the pin twice inside the ISR handler.
A larger pull-up resistor on the switch input.
questions.explanation: An RC filter into a Schmitt-trigger input slows and cleans the edge in hardware.

questions.prompt: On an ESP32 an interrupt handler occasionally crashes the board while the program writes to flash. What is the usual remedy?
options: Add delay(10) inside the handler to wait.
Lower the CPU clock.
Use a String for the handler name.
Mark it IRAM_ATTR so it runs from RAM.
questions.explanation: During a flash write the cache is disabled, so handler code must be in internal RAM: mark it IRAM_ATTR.

questions.prompt: A limit switch on a gantry must stop the motor immediately but the switch bounces for about 5 ms. Describe how you would read it (interrupt or polling, debounce method) and what the handler does.
rubric: Uses an interrupt on the first edge for immediate response and does the safe action (stop request) first, because debouncing must not delay a safety stop.
Keeps the ISR short: sets a volatile flag or stops the output, with no Serial or delay.
Debounces the release or re-arming with a time window (more than 5 ms, say 20 ms) or an RC filter, and keeps the hardware E-stop path independent of software.
